newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gehe bid spells end to Lloyds saga.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gehe bid spells end to Lloyds saga.

text.p: German group Gehe AG delivered on Friday what analysts predicted would be a knock-out blow in its year-long battle for control of British pharmaceutical chain Lloyds Chemists.

The drug wholesaler lifted its cash bid for Lloyds to 525 pence per share from 500 pence, valuing Lloyds at 684.1 million pounds ($1.15 billion) and trumping a rival bid from British drugs group Unichem.
The new and final offer opens clear blue water between the combined cash and share bid already on the table from Unichem.
Unichem has seen the value of its offer sink in line with its share price in recent weeks.

Ironically, the prospect that it would lose the bid battle saw Unichem's shares rise to close 9.5 to 255.5p on Friday, lifting the value of its bid to around 653 million pounds, as shareholders offered a collective sigh of relief that the pressure finally seemed to be off.
Sources close to Unichem would not comment on whether the British wholesaler would respond to Gehe's new offer. The company has until January 17 to improve its bid.
But the 14p rise in Lloyds' share price to 526.5 suggested that few in the City were expecting Gehe's price to be beaten.
Greig Middleton analyst Tony Cooper said Unichem would be hard pressed to come back with another offer, which would have to rely much more heavily on cash than its existing bid.

"(The bid of) 525 pence looks to me like a winning bid. Unichem doesn't have the firepower to match that," said Cooper, adding: "I didn't expect they'd go as high as this...it looks fairly fully priced."
Gehe said the offer represented 22 times Lloyds' earnings per share for the year ended June 30, 1996.

If Gehe wins the day, it will bring to an end an exhausting year-long struggle which has included a full inquiry by Britain's Monopolies and Mergers' Commission into the structure of the wholesale and retail market for pharmaceuticals.

"We do not believe that the continuing uncertainty is in the best interests of Lloyds Chemists and we have therefore decided to increase our offers with a view to bringing this matter to a conclusion," said Gehe management board chairman Dieter Kammerer.
Lloyds noted the uncertainty was having an adverse impact on its business when it posted first-half sales figures on Tuesday, with costs rising at it struggled to hold on to key staff.

Both Unichem and Gehe, which already owns British pharmacy chain AAH, have been actively adding drug retailing to their core wholesaling activities as a way of tying in trade and establishing a direct link with the public. ($1=.5950 Pound)
